objects.description: One bow-tie: the centre event that someone has decided is worth drawing, with the causes on its left and the consequences on its right. Whatever a domain is afraid of losing control of, it fills this role, and only the few fields beside the document mean the same in every domain.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The short human-readable label this bow-tie is known by in the register.

fields.name: top_event
fields.description: The centre of the bow-tie, stated precisely: the moment control of the hazard is lost. Threats are the ways it comes about and consequences are what follows, so a vague statement here makes both sides vague.

fields.name: hazard
fields.description: What could cause harm if control of it were lost. Often the same thing the top event is about, stated as a thing rather than as an event.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Who is accountable for this risk, as the mount's own reference to a person or a role. Opaque to this module. A risk cannot open without one.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Where the risk is in its life. The steps it may take between these is the module's rule, not the domain's, so the set is declared here.

fields.name: parent_pathway_id
fields.description: The pathway on another risk that this one drills into, which is how a branch of one bow-tie becomes a bow-tie of its own. Empty for a risk that stands alone. Fixed at creation, so the drill-down tree can never be rewired into a loop.

fields.name: doc
fields.description: Everything true of this risk that only its domain gives meaning to — a category, a business unit, a regulation it falls under. Queried in place by path rather than parsed per row, so anything domain-shaped lives in here rather than in a column of its own.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the row was created.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When the row was last written.

indexes.name: status_owner
indexes.description: The register listing, which filters on either or both.

indexes.name: parent_pathway
indexes.description: Finds the bow-ties that drill into one pathway.

objects.description: One way along one side of a bow-tie: a route by which the top event can come about, or a route by which its consequences unfold. Both sides have the same shape, so one object serves both and the side says which.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: risk_id
fields.description: The bow-tie this pathway belongs to. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: side
fields.description: Which half of the bow-tie the pathway is on. A threat leads to the top event and is guarded by preventive barriers; a consequence leads away from it and is guarded by mitigating ones. Fixed at creation, because every barrier standing on it takes its meaning from the side.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The short label for this route, as it would be written on the diagram.

fields.name: scenario
fields.description: A concrete example of the route being taken, in enough detail that someone could test a barrier against it.

fields.name: doc
fields.description: Everything true of this pathway that only its domain gives meaning to. Queried in place by path rather than parsed per row.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the row was created.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When the row was last written.

indexes.name: risk_side
indexes.description: Reads one half of one bow-tie.

objects.description: One measure an organisation operates — a technical safeguard, a procedure, an approval step. It is declared once and may stand on many pathways of many bow-ties, which is what makes a common-cause failure visible: the same control failing everywhere it was relied on.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the control is called. Unique, because two controls with one name make a failure impossible to attribute.

fields.name: description
fields.description: What the control does and what it is meant to stop, detect or limit.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Who operates the control, as the mount's own reference to a person, a role or a team. Opaque to this module. Not the same person as a risk's owner: one is accountable for the exposure and the other for the safeguard.

fields.name: doc
fields.description: Everything true of this control that only its domain gives meaning to — the system it runs in, the vendor, the standard it implements. Queried in place by path rather than parsed per row.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the row was created.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When the row was last written.

objects.description: One control standing on one pathway: the claim that this measure interrupts this route. The claim is what gets assessed, not the control, because a control that works in one place may not reach another.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: risk_id
fields.description: A copy of the bow-tie the pathway belongs to, held here so reading every barrier of a risk or every risk a control serves does not join through the pathway on each read.

fields.name: pathway_id
fields.description: The route the control stands on. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: control_id
fields.description: The measure standing there. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: position
fields.description: Where along the pathway the barrier stands, counting from the end furthest from the top event. Equal positions fall back to the order they were placed in.

fields.name: design
fields.description: Whether the control, as designed, addresses the specific route it is claimed to stand on. A judgement by whoever assesses it, not a measurement.

fields.name: coverage
fields.description: Whether the control is deployed across everything the route runs through — every application, user, agent and data source it applies to. A control on part of a route leaves the rest open. A judgement by whoever assesses it.

fields.name: maturity
fields.description: How far the barrier has got. Reaching tested or monitored needs at least one piece of evidence, so a barrier cannot claim to have been tried with nothing on record.

fields.name: retest_days
fields.description: How many days its latest evidence stays current. Once the latest evidence is older than this the barrier is stale: it is reported as a gap and its standing is no better than unproven. Zero means no window, so the evidence never goes stale.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: What is missing or weak about this barrier, and why it was rated as it was.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the row was created.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When the row was last written.

indexes.name: pathway_control
indexes.description: Finds the placement a pathway and a control identify, and stops one control standing twice on one route.

indexes.name: risk
indexes.description: Reads every barrier of one bow-tie.

indexes.name: control
indexes.description: Finds everywhere one control is relied on, which is the question a common-cause failure asks.

objects.description: One piece of proof about one barrier: a test that was run, a log that was read, an audit that was done. Append-only: a barrier that stopped working is shown by recording a further, failing piece of evidence, never by editing the earlier passing one, because a record that can be rewritten answers no question about the past.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: barrier_id
fields.description: The barrier this is evidence about.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: How the evidence was obtained. An incident is a real occurrence that showed the barrier working or failing, as opposed to a test of it.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: What the evidence showed. Partial means the barrier did some of what it was claimed to do, which is a finding and not a pass.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: What was done and what it showed, in enough detail that someone else could repeat it.

fields.name: reference
fields.description: Where the underlying material lives — a link, a ticket, a path — so the claim can be checked against the thing itself.

fields.name: recorded_by
fields.description: Who recorded it, supplied by the mount from the caller and never read from the request.

fields.name: recorded_at
fields.description: When the evidence was obtained, according to whoever obtained it. Takes the time the service received it when left out. This is the field evidence is ordered by.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When this service received it. Separate from recorded_at because evidence is often entered after the fact.

indexes.name: barrier_recorded
indexes.description: The query the module exists to answer: one barrier's evidence, in time order, newest last.

objects.description: One rating of one risk at one moment: how likely and how severe it is judged to be. Append-only, so the history of a rating is the history of how the organisation's view of the risk moved.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: risk_id
fields.description: The risk this rates.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Which exposure the rating describes. Inherent is the risk before any barrier is counted, residual is what remains with the barriers as they actually are, and target is what the owner has decided is tolerable.

fields.name: likelihood
fields.description: How likely the top event is, on a scale of 1 (rare) to 5 (almost certain).

fields.name: impact
fields.description: How severe the consequences are, on a scale of 1 (negligible) to 5 (severe).

fields.name: rationale
fields.description: Why the rating is what it is, so a later reader can disagree with the reasoning and not only the number.

fields.name: assessed_by
fields.description: Who made the rating, supplied by the mount from the caller and never read from the request.

fields.name: assessed_at
fields.description: When the rating was made, according to whoever made it. Takes the time the service received it when left out. This is the field ratings are ordered by.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When this service received it.

indexes.name: risk_kind_assessed
indexes.description: Reads the current rating of one kind, and its history, for one risk.

objects.description: One piece of work to close a gap: strengthen a barrier, test one, put one where none stands. It carries an owner and a due date, because a gap without them is an observation and not a commitment.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: risk_id
fields.description: The risk this work is for. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: barrier_id
fields.description: The barrier the work is about, when it is about one. Empty for work about the risk as a whole. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The short label for the work.

fields.name: description
fields.description: What is to be done, and what done looks like.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Who is to do it, as the mount's own reference to a person or a team. Opaque to this module.

fields.name: task_ref
fields.description: The task, in the task module, that tracks this work, as that module's own stable reference to it. Empty when the work is tracked only here. Opaque to this module unless the mount supplies a directory to check it against.

fields.name: due_at
fields.description: When it is due. Empty when no date has been agreed, which is itself reported as a gap.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Where the work is. Done and dropped are the end of the road: dropped says the gap is accepted as it is, and is told apart from done so that it is never mistaken for a fix.

fields.name: closed_at
fields.description: When the work was done or dropped. Empty while it is still going.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the row was created.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When the row was last written.

indexes.name: risk_status
indexes.description: Reads the open work of one bow-tie.

indexes.name: status_due
indexes.description: Finds the work that has gone past its date.
